scope: Manual supporting-fact labels for the three local snapshots, not generated answers or evaluation results. Regulatory questions refer to the downloaded 2026 summary, not independently reverified current law.

answerability_labels.supported: All requested information is supported by the listed source sections, including stated scope qualifications.
answerability_labels.partially_supported: Listed sections support general guidance, but the requested lake-specific detail is absent. Missing details must be acknowledged.
answerability_labels.unsupported: The snapshots provide no supporting evidence for the requested specific claim. Relevant sources and expected supporting facts are empty; do not substitute generic advice for an answer.

annotation_notes: Section headings are exact notebook metadata paths. Glossary terms are represented as subsections using the original definition labels.
All listed sections are needed for questions marked requires_multiple_sections; a single rule chunk does not replace its exceptions or qualifiers.
Supporting facts are paraphrased manual expectations, not source excerpts or model outputs. Explicit limitations describe absent evidence or source scope.
No retrieval or answer-quality scores have been measured. Any future scoring must account for overlapping chunks from the same section rather than assuming fixed node IDs.

questions.question: According to the guide, how does jaw position distinguish largemouth from smallmouth bass?

section_headings: Identifying, catching and handling fish species > Smallmouth and largemouth bass

expected_supporting_facts: The largemouth jaw hinge extends past the eye.
The smallmouth jaw hinge does not extend past the centre of the eye.

questions.question: How do the guide's typical largemouth and smallmouth habitats differ?

section_headings: Identifying, catching and handling fish species > Smallmouth and largemouth bass

expected_supporting_facts: Largemouth are more often associated with warm-water weed beds and ambush prey from weeds.
Smallmouth favour cool, clear water and rocky or sandy lake and river areas.
These are general habitat descriptions, not observations of bass locations in Rice Lake.

questions.question: What starting presentation and cover does the guide suggest for largemouth bass in weeds?

section_headings: Identifying, catching and handling fish species > Smallmouth and largemouth bass

expected_supporting_facts: Place bait or a lure at weed edges or openings.
The guide suggests real or artificial worms and working around logs, boulders, and other cover.
The advice does not guarantee a catch or establish a lake-specific best lure.

questions.question: What locations, hot-summer adjustment, and food preference does the guide mention for smallmouth bass?

section_headings: Identifying, catching and handling fish species > Smallmouth and largemouth bass

expected_supporting_facts: Look for rocky points, shoals, drop-offs, and submerged logs.
The guide suggests fishing deeper in hotter parts of summer but gives no numeric depth.
The guide identifies crayfish as a favourite food and says many bait or lure types may work.

questions.question: What gives a jig its action, and can it be paired with natural bait?

section_headings: Tackle and other gear > Types of lures > Jigs

expected_supporting_facts: A jig is described as a single hook with a weighted eye.
The angler supplies the motion; proper use creates a jerky vertical action.
Jigs can be used alone or with natural bait.

questions.question: What general advice does the guide give about time of day and choosing bait that resembles local food?

section_headings: Tips and techniques > Time of day
Tips and techniques > Imitate what the fish are eating

expected_supporting_facts: Many fish are more active at dawn or dusk, but fish can be caught at other times too.
Docks, weeds, log jams, and deeper water are suggested hiding areas.
Observe food such as dragonflies, minnows, and frogs and select imitating bait or lures.
This is general fish advice; it does not report a Rice Lake bite window.

questions.question: According to the guide, how should I handle a fish that I plan to release?

section_headings: Identifying, catching and handling fish species > Handling fish

expected_supporting_facts: Wet hands help avoid removing the protective slime coat, which protects against disease and infection.
Avoid touching the gills or eyes and return the fish to the water as soon as possible.
Use care around sharp spines and teeth.

questions.question: What are the 2026 Zone 17 zone-wide season and licence limits for largemouth and smallmouth bass combined, and do they override exceptions?

section_headings: Zone-wide seasons and limits
Zone-wide seasons and limits > Largemouth and smallmouth bass combined

expected_supporting_facts: The zone-wide bass season runs from the third Saturday in June through December 15.
The combined bass limits are S (sport) 6 and C (conservation) 2.
Zone-wide rules are subject to the listed species exceptions, waterbody exceptions, and fish sanctuaries.

questions.question: Under the 2026 summary, does a Zone 17 sport licence allow six largemouth plus six smallmouth bass?

section_headings: Glossary of terms > Aggregate (combined) limits
Zone-wide seasons and limits > Largemouth and smallmouth bass combined

expected_supporting_facts: The Zone 17 sport limit is six bass combined, not six of each species.
An aggregate limit applies to the combination; separate limits cannot be retained for each species.
Zone-specific exceptions and sanctuaries still apply.

questions.question: In the downloaded summary, how does a closed season differ from an open season with a zero limit if I intend to release every fish?

section_headings: Glossary of terms > Catch and Release Seasons
Glossary of terms > Open seasons

expected_supporting_facts: Targeting a species in its closed season is prohibited even with an intention to release it.
An open season with a zero limit permits targeting but requires release under the applicable release rules.
Fish accidentally caught during a closed season must be immediately released.

questions.question: Do fish given to a friend count toward my daily catch limit, and does possession include fish in storage?

section_headings: Glossary of terms > Catch and possession limits

expected_supporting_facts: Fish given away count toward the catcher's daily catch limit, including gifts within the fishing party.
Possession includes fish on hand, in cold storage, in transit, or elsewhere.
Possession limits normally equal one day's catch limit unless otherwise specified.

questions.question: According to the downloaded 2026 summary, during an otherwise open Zone 17 bass season outside sanctuaries, what conditions apply to a sport-license angler selectively live-releasing bass from a boat after reaching six retained bass?

section_headings: Catch and retain rules
Glossary of terms > Livewell
Zone-wide seasons and limits > Largemouth and smallmouth bass combined

expected_supporting_facts: The boat provision allows catching, holding, and selective live release of bass subject to its conditions; it does not permit holding more than six combined bass at any time on a sport licence.
Fish must comply with applicable size limits and be held in a livewell with a mechanical aerator operating continuously.
A livewell must be attached to or part of a boat, hold at least 46 litres, and have water-exchange capacity and aeration while holding live fish.
Fish condition must be monitored; only fish expected to survive may be released, and fish not live-released count toward catch and possession limits.
Zone 17's combined sport bass limit is six, subject to exceptions and sanctuaries.

questions.question: Does the 2026 Zone 17 zone-wide walleye season allow walleye fishing in Lake Scugog or the described Scugog River waters?

section_headings: Zone-wide seasons and limits > Walleye and sauger combined
Waterbody exceptions

expected_supporting_facts: The zone-wide walleye/sauger season runs from the second Saturday in May through November 15.
The Lake Scugog and Scugog River waterbody exception closes walleye fishing all year in the described waters.
The exception includes waters south of Highway 7A, Blackstock Creek, Nonquon River, Scugog River to the Trent Severn Dam in Lindsay, Mariposa Brook, and East Cross Creek.
The waterbody closure overrides the zone-wide season there.

questions.question: Under the 2026 summary, may I target bass on November 20 within 100 metres of either side of the Bridgenorth Causeway on Chemong Lake just because the zone-wide bass season is open?

section_headings: Zone-wide seasons and limits > Largemouth and smallmouth bass combined
Fish sanctuaries > No fishing - January 1 to Friday before the second Saturday in May and November 16 to December 31
Glossary of terms > Fish sanctuaries

expected_supporting_facts: The zone-wide bass season extends to December 15, but sanctuary restrictions take precedence.
The listed Chemong Lake sanctuary covers 100 metres on both sides of Bridgenorth Causeway on County Road 16 in Smith and Ennismore Townships.
That sanctuary is closed from November 16 through December 31, which includes November 20.
No fishing of any kind is permitted in a fish sanctuary during its closure, including catch-and-release bass targeting.

questions.question: How do the 2026 walleye limits and size restriction for the described Balsam and Mitchell Lake waters differ from Zone 17's zone-wide rule, and which season applies?

section_headings: Zone-wide seasons and limits > Walleye and sauger combined
Species exceptions > Walleye

expected_supporting_facts: The zone-wide combined walleye/sauger limits are S 4 and C 1, with fish between 35 and 50 centimetres.
The walleye species exception for the described Balsam and Mitchell Lake waters specifies S 3 and C 1, with none between 37 and 55 centimetres.
That exception uses the zone-wide season: second Saturday in May through November 15.
The exception describes connected waters as well as the named lakes; its geographic descriptions must be retained.

questions.question: Does keeping bass alive in a livewell on a boat mean I can tow them home alive overland without a permit under the downloaded summary?

section_headings: Glossary of terms > Livewell
Transporting sport fish

expected_supporting_facts: The summary prohibits transporting live fish overland without a permit, except baitfish; bass are not covered by that baitfish exception.
Livewells should be drained and emptied, including live fish, before overland transport.
Sport fish transported overland must be dead and should be on ice, rather than in a water-filled livewell.

questions.question: What bait-management zone does the downloaded Zone 17 chapter identify, and what does it say about crossing bait-management-zone boundaries with baitfish or leeches?

section_headings: General information

expected_supporting_facts: FMZ 17 is part of the Southern Bait Management Zone.
Live or dead baitfish or leeches may not be transported into or out of a bait-management zone.
The stated exception is for baitfish and leeches that are both dead and preserved; dead alone does not satisfy that wording.
The chapter refers readers to the separate Bait section for more detail; that section is not among these three snapshots.

questions.question: What exact depth in metres should I fish for smallmouth bass on Rice Lake this hot afternoon, and what general guidance do these sources offer?

section_headings: Identifying, catching and handling fish species > Smallmouth and largemouth bass

expected_supporting_facts: The guide suggests deeper water in hotter parts of summer and identifies rocky points, shoals, drop-offs, and submerged logs as places to look.
This general guidance does not establish a numeric depth or current Rice Lake fish location.
missing_evidence: Current Rice Lake water temperatures, fish observations, and location-specific depth information.
